description: Native Windows MANUAL/BLOCKED qualification items derived from the cited review reports. Automated CTest PASS is not a substitute.

items.title: Interactive full workflow on a real desktop with a real mouse/keyboard
steps: Launch MViewer on a real Windows desktop (not an offscreen or headless session).
Exercise the product loop with the mouse and keyboard: Browse a folder, open Viewer, next/previous, zoom/pan, Compare a pair, Analyze, Export, FileOps.
M51 target-machine pass also repeats Browse -> Select -> Compare -> Zoom/ROI -> Export on this desktop.
items.expected: The interactive full workflow completes with real input. Green CTest runs (m46_browse_tests, m46_repository_tests, workflow_ux_tests) are not a substitute for this row.
automationHints: m46_browse_tests and m46_repository_tests cover race safety of viewer/compare destroy and A->B->A
workflow_ux_tests covers the offscreen Browse/Compare loop

items.title: Perceived smoothness / flicker / zoom feel during the loop
prerequisites: UX Review Agent observing the live GUI
steps: Repeat the Browse -> Viewer -> Compare -> Analyze -> Export loop on the target desktop.
Watch layout changes, zoom, and mode switches for flicker, a white frame, or a jump.
Judge zoom feel (Fit / 100% / 200% / free zoom) and focus continuity / stale-state perception (M51 soak list).
items.expected: No flicker, white frame, or jump. Zoom geometry feels correct. UX Review Agent on the target desktop; offscreen tests do not cover perceived smoothness.
automationHints: docs/beta_checklist.md pass criteria: no waiting, no flicker, no zoom error, no state desync

items.title: 100% DPI run
steps: Set the primary display scaling to 100% and sign in so the session uses that DPI.
Launch MViewer and run Browse, Viewer zoom/pan, and Compare on this display.
items.expected: Layout, hit-testing, and zoom geometry stay correct at 100% DPI. Requires an interactive display session.
automationHints: Wizard records the detected session scaling when obtainable

items.title: 125% DPI run
steps: Set the primary display scaling to 125% (fractional scaling) and sign in so the session uses that DPI.
Launch MViewer and run Browse, Viewer zoom/pan, and Compare on this display.
items.expected: Layout, hit-testing, and zoom geometry stay correct at 125% DPI. Requires an interactive display session.
automationHints: Wizard records the detected session scaling when obtainable

items.title: 150% DPI run
steps: Set the primary display scaling to 150% and sign in so the session uses that DPI.
Launch MViewer and run Browse, Viewer zoom/pan, and Compare on this display.
items.expected: Layout, hit-testing, and zoom geometry stay correct at 150% DPI. Requires an interactive display session.
automationHints: Wizard records the detected session scaling when obtainable

items.title: 200% DPI run
steps: Set the primary display scaling to 200% and sign in so the session uses that DPI.
Launch MViewer and run Browse, Viewer zoom/pan, and Compare on this display.
items.expected: Layout, hit-testing, and zoom geometry stay correct at 200% DPI. Requires an interactive display session.
automationHints: Wizard records the detected session scaling when obtainable

items.title: Mixed-DPI dual monitor (per-monitor DPI)
prerequisites: two physical displays with different DPI
steps: Attach two physical monitors configured with different scaling (per-monitor DPI).
Launch MViewer, move the window between the two displays, and resize it on each.
Repeat Browse / Viewer zoom / Compare after the move. M59 also asks for mixed-DPI monitor moves.
items.expected: Per-monitor DPI is honored. The offscreen platform cannot create mixed-DPI monitors; this row stays BLOCKED without two physical displays at different DPI.
automationHints: Wizard auto-blocks when fewer than two monitors are detected

items.title: Physical ICC profile changes while running (profile switch / unplug)

also.row: 9. How are profile changes made safe?

steps: Launch MViewer displaying a color-critical image on a real monitor with an installed ICC profile.
While it is running, switch the monitor ICC profile and/or unplug and replug the display.
Confirm Viewer/Compare cancel in-flight display work and refresh against the new target (M59 DisplayColorContext generation).
items.expected: Profile switch or unplug does not crash, black-frame, or mutate source bytes. Malformed/missing target falls back to sRGB. ICC parsing itself is covered by iccprofile_tests / m36_display_tests.
automationHints: iccprofile_tests and m36_display_tests cover embedded-profile display copies
m59_color_managed_tests cover generation invalidation in automation

items.title: FileOps across two real physical volumes (copy/move with cross-volume fallback)
steps: Open a folder on volume A that contains images MViewer can browse.
Copy and move files to a folder on volume B (a second writable physical volume).
Confirm the cross-volume fallback path is used and the operation completes or is cancelled cleanly.
items.expected: Copy/move across two real physical volumes succeeds via the cross-volume fallback. A single-volume host is BLOCKED. The code path itself is covered by test_commandstack 'cross-volume rename fallback' (fault-injected adapter).
automationHints: test_commandstack covers the fault-injected cross-volume rename fallback

items.title: Native Windows open/save dialogs (file dialogs with shell UI)
prerequisites: interactive Windows desktop with shell UI
steps: From MViewer, invoke the native Open and Save dialogs (open folder / open files / export save).
Navigate the shell UI, including a path with spaces, and confirm/cancel each dialog.
items.expected: Native Windows file dialogs appear and work. Interactive native dialogs cannot be driven offscreen; dialog-less paths are covered by mainwindow_commandstack_acceptance.
automationHints: mainwindow_commandstack_acceptance covers non-interactive dialog-less paths

items.title: Long paths (> 260 chars, extended-length)
prerequisites: a real volume with long-path support enabled
steps: Confirm the OS long-path policy is enabled on this volume (LongPathsEnabled).
Create or copy an image under a path whose full length exceeds 260 characters.
Open that folder in MViewer and browse / open / export using the long path.
items.expected: Paths longer than 260 characters work when the OS long-path policy is enabled. test_commandstack covers cross-volume/Unicode but not the OS long-path policy.
automationHints: Wizard reports HKLM FileSystem LongPathsEnabled
test_commandstack covers Unicode paths, not OS long-path policy

items.title: Special filenames (leading dots, trailing spaces, reserved names)
prerequisites: a volume whose policy allows the special names under test
steps: On a real volume, create test images whose names have a leading dot and, where the volume allows it, a trailing space.
Where the volume policy allows reserved names (CON, NUL, ...), create or attempt those names too.
Browse, open, rename, and undo in MViewer.
items.expected: Leading-dot names work. Trailing spaces and reserved names (CON/NUL) are volume-policy dependent; record what the volume accepted and how MViewer behaved. Unicode/Chinese/emoji rename round-trip is already automated (test_commandstack).
automationHints: test_commandstack covers Unicode dir + Chinese/emoji rename round-trip

items.title: Long session RSS/handles on the target desktop
prerequisites: interactive target desktop available for a multi-hour session
steps: Launch MViewer on the target desktop and use Browse / Viewer / Compare / Analyze / Export over a multi-hour interactive session.
Record RSS and handle counts at start, during use, and after returning to idle.
Watch for leaks, a stranded busy cursor, and stale UI state (M51: focus continuity, stale-state perception, resource behavior).
items.expected: The multi-hour interactive session remains usable; RSS/handles are observed on target hardware. The automated short soak (m46_workflow_soak) proves convergence mechanics only; m46_workflow_soak --extended is the longer automated form, not this human observation.
automationHints: m46_workflow_soak CTest short form: pools -> 0, RSS <= max(128 MiB, 15%), handles <= +64
extended automated form: m46_workflow_soak --extended

items.title: Clean-machine install, upgrade, Explorer Open With, association launch, and uninstall
prerequisites: shipping portable ZIP and NSIS installer artifacts
steps: Install both shipping artifacts (portable ZIP launch and NSIS installer) on a clean Windows machine.
Exercise each native association (.mvws, .mvproj, Explorer Open With / file launch) with paths containing spaces and Unicode.
Repeat Browse -> Select -> Compare -> Zoom/ROI -> Export from those launches.
Upgrade over the installed copy, then uninstall and confirm current associations are removed and the obsolete .mviewer registration is not left behind.
Record OS build, display scaling, GPU, driver, ICC profile, storage type, and exact artifact hashes.
items.expected: Install, upgrade, association launch, and clean uninstall work on a physical clean Windows machine. Uninstall removes current associations without leaving the obsolete .mviewer registration. The package gate does not replace this row.
automationHints: release_contract_tests and package_release.ps1 cover the unpacked payload, PE version, and SHA256SUMS
NSIS does not register the obsolete .mviewer extension

items.title: UNC/network shares, removable volumes, and interruption during Sidecar/import/export
prerequisites: a UNC or network share, and/or a removable volume
ability to interrupt or reconnect the share during Sidecar/import/export
steps: Open a folder on a UNC/network share and on a removable volume and browse images.
Run Sidecar / import / export against those paths.
Interrupt or reconnect the share or volume during those operations and record the outcome.
items.expected: UNC, removable volumes, and interruption/reconnection during Sidecar/import/export are qualified on the target machine. No automated green result is claimed for these target-dependent rows.
automationHints: Automated fixtures cover ASCII, spaces, Chinese, emoji, quoted paths, and Unicode workspace/project names

items.title: GPU/driver combination native display
prerequisites: the target machine GPU and driver under test
steps: Record the GPU name and driver version (the wizard captures these when CIM is available).
Launch MViewer on this GPU/driver combination and run Browse, Viewer, and Compare.
Note any driver-specific display or compositor defects.
items.expected: Native display works on the recorded GPU/driver combination. The target-machine pass records GPU and driver alongside OS build and display scaling.
automationHints: Wizard records Win32_VideoController Name and DriverVersion when available

items.title: Long-session GIF/WebP playback feel on a native GUI
steps: Open an animated GIF and an animated WebP in the Viewer on a real desktop.
Play, pause, restart, and step frames (, / .) over a long interactive session.
Watch playback feel, zoom/pan preservation across frames, and whether a corrupt frame pauses without a busy retry loop.
items.expected: Physical native GUI playback feel is qualified. A slow decode is caught up/skipped; a corrupt requested frame pauses and reports failure without crossing the Viewer boundary. Deterministic plugin decode is covered by m57_multiframe_decoder_tests.
automationHints: m57_multiframe_decoder_tests covers real qgif/qwebp/qtiff fixtures and bounded-stall catch-up

items.title: Hostile GIF disposal / dirty-rectangle corpus
steps: Open GIF samples that use hostile disposal methods and dirty rectangles.
Play and step frames, including cases with transparency.
items.expected: Composed frames remain usable (qgif's composed QImage is the display source). The deterministic real-plugin fixture verifies distinct composed colors; a hostile disposal/dirty-rectangle corpus remains manual follow-up.
automationHints: m57_multiframe_decoder_tests verifies distinct composed colors on the real qgif plugin

items.title: 100MP multi-page TIFF RSS / soak
prerequisites: a 100MP-class multi-page TIFF on the target machine
steps: Open a 100MP multi-page TIFF in the Viewer.
Navigate pages without requesting every page up front.
Record RSS while stepping pages and after returning to idle.
items.expected: Page selection is on-demand and does not enumerate or decode all pages. Physical 100MP multi-page RSS was not available in the M57 automated run; the M53 source-backed large-image contract remains the governing path.
automationHints: M53 source-backed large-image contract governs 100MP-class TIFF display

items.title: Physical monitor-profile / LUT verification

also.row: 8. How is the monitor profile obtained?

prerequisites: a representative physical monitor with a known ICC/LUT
steps: On a real Windows host, display an embedded-profile image (for example AdobeRGB) and an untagged sRGB image.
Confirm the UI asks Windows GetICMProfileW for the current window device context and uses that monitor profile as the presentation target.
Capture compositor screenshots as evidence (M59 remaining manual list).
Confirm Pixel Inspector still samples source pixels, not the monitor-converted display raster.
items.expected: Presentation targets the currently attached physical monitor profile. Errors, unavailable profiles, and non-Windows builds fall back to sRGB. No automated claim is made for a particular panel LUT. Source bytes are not mutated; Inspector samples the source ImageFrame.
automationHints: m59_color_managed_tests cover CPU/GPU parity, malformed ICC fallback, and source-buffer snapshots
M48 already proves embedded ICC is applied on display copies only

items.title: HDR policy and tone mapping on a physical HDR monitor
steps: Attach an HDR-capable monitor and enable HDR in Windows.
Launch MViewer and display ordinary SDR sources (untagged and ICC-tagged).
Record whether presentation stays an 8-bit SDR buffer and whether the HDR policy is explicit (no silent HDR tone-mapping claim).
items.expected: HDR policy and tone mapping remain a manual qualification. The display ImageData remains an explicit 8-bit SDR presentation buffer; analysis/source data is not down-converted in place. No automated HDR claim is made.
automationHints: M59 Q14: display ImageData remains an explicit 8-bit SDR presentation buffer

items.title: Linked ROI pointer feel on a physical desktop
prerequisites: interactive native GUI with a real pointing device
steps: Open Compare on a real desktop and create a linked ROI with a right-button drag in Grid, Split, Overlay, Swipe, and Checkerboard.
Move the ROI by dragging inside it and resize from edges and corners.
Judge pointer feel: overlay tracking, handle hitting, and whether statistics wait until release.
items.expected: Pointer feel is qualified on a native GUI. Automated tests send real right-button events but do not judge perceived tracking. Programmatic applyROI() is not the sole evidence (M61 Q14).
automationHints: m61_roi_workflow_tests and workflow_ux_tests send real right-button events to production widgets

items.title: ROI overlay contrast on a physical calibrated or HDR monitor
prerequisites: a physical calibrated and/or HDR monitor
steps: Display Compare with a linked ROI on a calibrated and/or HDR monitor.
Confirm the high-contrast overlay, label, and handles remain readable against the image.
When Analysis is hidden, confirm the compact HUD stays readable and does not cover the ROI center.
items.expected: ROI overlay contrast is readable on a physical calibrated/HDR monitor. This is a manual boundary; automated widget tests do not judge physical contrast.
automationHints: m61_roi_workflow_tests covers hidden-panel HUD geometry in automation
